case_context.legal_issue: Whether the proscription orders infringed the petitioner's fundamental right to freedom of association under Article 14(1)(c).
case_context.petitioner_claim: The petitioner claimed that the proscription of the J.V.P. infringed his right to associate freely as a member of a recognized political party.
case_context.respondent_argument: The Attorney-General argued that the President's immunity under Article 35(1) barred the proceedings and that the proscription was lawful under Emergency Regulations, not subject to challenge against the Attorney-General.
key_facts: The petitioner was a member of the J.V.P., a recognized political party.
The J.V.P. was proscribed by the President under Emergency Regulations.
The petitioner and members were prevented from functioning as a political party.
The petitioner alleged mala fide motives behind the proscription.
The petitioner cited infringement of Article 14(1)(c) rights.

reasoning.interpretation_summary: The court recognized the right to freedom of association under Article 14(1)(c) but held that the President's immunity under Article 35(1) prevented proceedings against the Attorney-General since the proscription was not under powers assigned under Article 44(2).
reasoning.application_to_facts: The proscription prevented the petitioner and others from associating as a political party, but the court dismissed the petition on procedural grounds related to immunity and proper party.
principles_established: Absolute immunity of the President under Article 35(1) applies to acts not under Article 44(2).
Proceedings against the President for acts under Article 44(2) must be against the Attorney-General.
Proscription under Emergency Regulations is not an act under Article 44(2).

outcome.holding: The petition alleging infringement of Article 14(1)(c) rights was dismissed for lack of proper party and jurisdiction.

link_explanation.why_this_clause_matters: Article 14(1)(c) was central to the petitioner's claim that the proscription infringed freedom of association, but the court's immunity and procedural ruling prevented relief.

evidence.evidence_excerpt: The petitioner claimed infringement of freedom of association under Article 14(1)(c) due to proscription; the court held the Attorney-General was not the proper respondent and dismissed the petition.
